# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1765._

> ℹ️ **12 resolved thread(s) excluded; 10 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vfu` — app UI can't reach the spilled request detail

**Fixed** on this head (commit `3f4ef0ad03`).

The app Request tab now surfaces the same pointer the CLI `/trajectory inspect` renders:

- `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_details_tabs.dart` (`_requestPage`) gained a **"Request blob"** row (`strings.requestSpillFile`) rendered whenever `detail.spillFile != null`, grouped with the prompt/manifest hash pointer rows. A new fixture (`spilledAssistant` in `packages/fa_ui/test/trajectory/fixture_details.dart`) pins it: `packages/fa_ui/test/trajectory/trajectory_details_test.dart`, test *"gh-1745: a spilled request names its blob; the stub messages carry no dangling colon"*.
- The tab's inline per-message list skips the empty preview `Text` for stub messages (the text rides the blob) instead of rendering blank lines.
- The dangling-colon renderer is gone from both surfaces the thread named:
  - `_requestSummaryText` (copy-to-clipboard) — new `_requestStubLine` helper emits `role · N chars` with no `: ` tail when `preview.isEmpty`;
  - `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart` Markdown export — same guard; spilled sessions export `- \`user\` 10 chars` (test: `test/trajectory/trajectory_export_test.dart`, *"gh-1745: a spilled request summary exports without dangling colons"*).

Resolution choice: we surface the `spillFile` row rather than resolving the blob content in-tab — the details tabs are pure widgets over the snapshot with no `ExecutionEnv` reach, and the pointer keeps parity with the CLI viewer. Scoping the PR to the CLI host is unnecessary now that the app side has its pointer.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: "Closes #1745" — but `shell_job_registry` (216 MB of the cited ~875 MB) is untouched**

The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. This PR remediates only `model_request_summary`; nothing here touches `shell_job_registry`, so a marathon session still grows unboundedly — just ~4× slower — while the issue auto-closes.

The ticket's Proposed Fix section only describes the `model_request_summary` remediation, so the implementation matches the fix plan — please just confirm the `shell_job_registry` half has a follow-up issue (or extend the blob/TTL policy to it here) so "Closes #1745" doesn't retire the ticket with a quarter of the cited disk growth still open.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `TrajectorySection.requestBlobMaxBytes` is dead code — use it**

The getter (`cli_config.dart:129`) is never referenced: both hosts re-derive the byte budget inline —

- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart`: `maxBytes: config.trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`
- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_lifecycle.dart`: `maxBytes: trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`

Two copies of the MB→bytes shift with the canonical one unused. Either thread `section.requestBlobMaxBytes` through `CliConfig`/`AgentCliConfig` (a `trajectoryRequestBlobMaxBytes` field) so both call sites consume the getter, or drop the getter.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the config SAVE path (`_trajectoryYaml`) is untested**

The new tests cover parsing (`requestBlobs` defaults, knob validation, strict unknown keys) and `loadProjectTrajectorySection`, but nothing round-trips a save: `_trajectoryYaml()` writes `requestBlobs: false` / non-default knobs only-when-non-default (defaults never written — the file-stays-minimal convention). One assertion like:

```dart
final saved = config.copyWith(trajectoryRequestBlobs: false).toYamlString();
expect(saved, contains('requestBlobs: false'));
```

would pin the save shape (the sibling sections each have one). Low risk — the parse tests would catch a malformed key on the next load — but the asymmetry is free to close.

The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. ### 3. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:2a084fc4` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

### 4. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:c9b477ec` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

💡 **SUGGESTION: `TrajectorySection.requestBlobMaxBytes` is dead code — use it**

The getter (`cli_config.dart:129`) is never referenced: both hosts re-derive the byte budget inline —

- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart`: `maxBytes: config.trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`
- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_lifecycle.dart`: `maxBytes: trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`

Two copies of the MB→bytes shift with the canonical one unused. Either thread `section.requestBlobMaxBytes` through `CliConfig`/`AgentCliConfig` (a `trajectoryRequestBlobMaxBytes` field) so both call sites consume the getter, or drop the getter.

### 5. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:b7059339` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

💡 **SUGGESTION: the config SAVE path (`_trajectoryYaml`) is untested**

The new tests cover parsing (`requestBlobs` defaults, knob validation, strict unknown keys) and `loadProjectTrajectorySection`, but nothing round-trips a save: `_trajectoryYaml()` writes `requestBlobs: false` / non-default knobs only-when-non-default (defaults never written — the file-stays-minimal convention). One assertion like:

```dart
final saved = config.copyWith(trajectoryRequestBlobs: false).toYamlString();
expect(saved, contains('requestBlobs: false'));
```

would pin the save shape (the sibling sections each have one). Low risk — the parse tests would catch a malformed key on the next load — but the asymmetry is free to close.

### 6. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:2b626cf5` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

### 7. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:c44f03a2` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

Verified: `grep -rn spillFile packages/fa_ui/lib flutter_app/lib` finds only this writer side.

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1765
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1765
- **Title**: gh-1745 [PERF] Marathon session files grow to 1GB due to unrotated model_request_summary raw prompt dumps
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1745` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 22
- **Additions**: +1616
- **Deletions**: -62
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T20:38:25Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T00:44:30Z

## PR Description

Refs #1745 (does not close it — see Scope below)
### What changed
- `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`; the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes + rotates the blobs: 50 MB/session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first with the newest always kept; wired into both persist hosts (CLI + app service). `/trajectory inspect` names the blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON; `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (+ `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`, strict section) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path — the capture is never lost, never a crash (same shape as tool-result spilling).
- Replay-safe: the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` basis survives the stubbing; old sessions render as before; `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the blob payload.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

### Scope (gh-1745 closing intent)
- This PR ships the issue's *Proposed Fix* tier: the `model_request_summary` blob offload (658.75 MB of the cited session) with per-session rotation (50 MB / 30-day TTL) plus a boot-time sweep of ended sessions' dirs.
- The **delta-encoding tier** from the issue's own triage comment (99% duplicate payloads, est. 345 MB → ~3.4 MB) is deliberately **not** in this PR — the closing keyword is dropped (`Refs`, not `Closes`) so #1745 stays open for that work.
- The `shell_job_registry` half (215.92 MB) is already bounded for new runs by #1594's persist-window + dedupe — no further work here.

<details><summary>Record flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[".fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json"]
  STORE -->|strip| REC["model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile"]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT["TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept"]
```
</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1765._

> ℹ️ **12 resolved thread(s) excluded; 10 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vfu` — app UI can't reach the spilled request detail

**Fixed** on this head (commit `3f4ef0ad03`).

The app Request tab now surfaces the same pointer the CLI `/trajectory inspect` renders:

- `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_details_tabs.dart` (`_requestPage`) gained a **"Request blob"** row (`strings.requestSpillFile`) rendered whenever `detail.spillFile != null`, grouped with the prompt/manifest hash pointer rows. A new fixture (`spilledAssistant` in `packages/fa_ui/test/trajectory/fixture_details.dart`) pins it: `packages/fa_ui/test/trajectory/trajectory_details_test.dart`, test *"gh-1745: a spilled request names its blob; the stub messages carry no dangling colon"*.
- The tab's inline per-message list skips the empty preview `Text` for stub messages (the text rides the blob) instead of rendering blank lines.
- The dangling-colon renderer is gone from both surfaces the thread named:
  - `_requestSummaryText` (copy-to-clipboard) — new `_requestStubLine` helper emits `role · N chars` with no `: ` tail when `preview.isEmpty`;
  - `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart` Markdown export — same guard; spilled sessions export `- \`user\` 10 chars` (test: `test/trajectory/trajectory_export_test.dart`, *"gh-1745: a spilled request summary exports without dangling colons"*).

Resolution choice: we surface the `spillFile` row rather than resolving the blob content in-tab — the details tabs are pure widgets over the snapshot with no `ExecutionEnv` reach, and the pointer keeps parity with the CLI viewer. Scoping the PR to the CLI host is unnecessary now that the app side has its pointer.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: "Closes #1745" — but `shell_job_registry` (216 MB of the cited ~875 MB) is untouched**

The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. This PR remediates only `model_request_summary`; nothing here touches `shell_job_registry`, so a marathon session still grows unboundedly — just ~4× slower — while the issue auto-closes.

The ticket's Proposed Fix section only describes the `model_request_summary` remediation, so the implementation matches the fix plan — please just confirm the `shell_job_registry` half has a follow-up issue (or extend the blob/TTL policy to it here) so "Closes #1745" doesn't retire the ticket with a quarter of the cited disk growth still open.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `TrajectorySection.requestBlobMaxBytes` is dead code — use it**

The getter (`cli_config.dart:129`) is never referenced: both hosts re-derive the byte budget inline —

- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart`: `maxBytes: config.trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`
- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_lifecycle.dart`: `maxBytes: trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`

Two copies of the MB→bytes shift with the canonical one unused. Either thread `section.requestBlobMaxBytes` through `CliConfig`/`AgentCliConfig` (a `trajectoryRequestBlobMaxBytes` field) so both call sites consume the getter, or drop the getter.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the config SAVE path (`_trajectoryYaml`) is untested**

The new tests cover parsing (`requestBlobs` defaults, knob validation, strict unknown keys) and `loadProjectTrajectorySection`, but nothing round-trips a save: `_trajectoryYaml()` writes `requestBlobs: false` / non-default knobs only-when-non-default (defaults never written — the file-stays-minimal convention). One assertion like:

```dart
final saved = config.copyWith(trajectoryRequestBlobs: false).toYamlString();
expect(saved, contains('requestBlobs: false'));
```

would pin the save shape (the sibling sections each have one). Low risk — the parse tests would catch a malformed key on the next load — but the asymmetry is free to close.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: unrelated reformat of `_CliMessageCapPolicy.learnedCapFor`**

This hunk (`agent_cli.dart`, `_CliMessageCapPolicy`) is pure whitespace/line-wrapping churn — no behavior change, not required by gh-1745. It widens the diff for anyone bisecting or re-running this file's history. Revert it so the PR stays single-purpose (the local `dart format` version here disagrees with the committed style anyway — the pre-existing lines around it trigger the same delta, so it's a formatter-version artifact, not a real lint fix).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (re-raised, still valid on this head): spilled request detail is unreachable from the app UI — only the CLI got a viewer**

This hunk wires spilling into the app host and stubs the buffered detail to role+chars (`preview: ''`, no blocks, `spillFile` pointer), but the app-side readers were not updated:

- `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_details_tabs.dart` `_requestPage` renders `message.preview` (now always `''` for every new session) and `message.blocks` (now always empty) — with no `spillFile` row and no blob resolution. Verified: `grep -rn spillFile packages/fa_ui/lib flutter_app/lib` finds only this writer side.
- `_requestSummaryText` (the Request tab's copy-to-clipboard) renders `'${message.role} · N chars: '` + empty preview → every line ends in a dangling `: `.
- `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart` (Markdown export, per-message list) has the same dangling-colon shape for spilled sessions.

Net effect: for every new app-hosted session the per-message drill-in data still exists on disk (the blob) but is unreachable from the app — a quiet UX regression the CLI half of this PR solved for itself (`/trajectory inspect` names the blob). Old sessions keep rendering (inline previews intact), so this is degradation, not breakage — hence not blocking.

Please add the same pointer to the app Request tab (a `spillFile` row, or resolve the blob via the exported `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore.readDetail`), and fix the two `': '` dangling-colon renderers for the stubbed shape (guard on `preview.isEmpty`).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (re-raised, narrowed after reading the linked issue): "Closes #1745" vs the issue's own triage plan**

The linked issue (github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness#1745, Problem Summary, read this run) cites two unrotated record kinds: `model_request_summary` at **658.75 MB** (1101 records) and `shell_job_registry` at **215.92 MB** (2487 records). This PR remediates the dominant first one — good — but two scope facts are worth settling before the issue auto-closes:

1. The issue's own triage comment (ai-teammate, 2026-10-21) demotes exactly this remediation: *"blob offload + per-session TTL/rotation — the original proposal — moves to second tier (long audit retention), not a prerequisite"* in favor of delta-encoding consecutive summaries as the core fix (measured 99% duplicate payloads, estimated 345 MB → ~3.4 MB). # Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vfu` — app UI can't reach the spilled request detail

**Fixed** on this head (commit `3f4ef0ad03`).

The app Request tab now surfaces the same pointer the CLI `/trajectory inspect` renders:

- `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_details_tabs.dart` (`_requestPage`) gained a **"Request blob"** row (`strings.requestSpillFile`) rendered whenever `detail.spillFile != null`, grouped with the prompt/manifest hash pointer rows. A new fixture (`spilledAssistant` in `packages/fa_ui/test/trajectory/fixture_details.dart`) pins it: `packages/fa_ui/test/trajectory/trajectory_details_test.dart`, test *"gh-1745: a spilled request names its blob; the stub messages carry no dangling colon"*.
- The tab's inline per-message list skips the empty preview `Text` for stub messages (the text rides the blob) instead of rendering blank lines.
- The dangling-colon renderer is gone from both surfaces the thread named:
  - `_requestSummaryText` (copy-to-clipboard) — new `_requestStubLine` helper emits `role · N chars` with no `: ` tail when `preview.isEmpty`;
  - `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart` Markdown export — same guard; spilled sessions export `- \`user\` 10 chars` (test: `test/trajectory/trajectory_export_test.dart`, *"gh-1745: a spilled request summary exports without dangling colons"*).

Resolution choice: we surface the `spillFile` row rather than resolving the blob content in-tab — the details tabs are pure widgets over the snapshot with no `ExecutionEnv` reach, and the pointer keeps parity with the CLI viewer. Scoping the PR to the CLI host is unnecessary now that the app side has its pointer.

### 2. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:6aad8c42` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: "Closes #1745" — but `shell_job_registry` (216 MB of the cited ~875 MB) is untouched**

The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. This PR remediates only `model_request_summary`; nothing here touches `shell_job_registry`, so a marathon session still grows unboundedly — just ~4× slower — while the issue auto-closes.

The ticket's Proposed Fix section only describes the `model_request_summary` remediation, so the implementation matches the fix plan — please just confirm the `shell_job_registry` half has a follow-up issue (or extend the blob/TTL policy to it here) so "Closes #1745" doesn't retire the ticket with a quarter of the cited disk growth still open.

### 3. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:2a084fc4` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

### 4. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:c9b477ec` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

💡 **SUGGESTION: `TrajectorySection.requestBlobMaxBytes` is dead code — use it**

The getter (`cli_config.dart:129`) is never referenced: both hosts re-derive the byte budget inline —

- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart`: `maxBytes: config.trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`
- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_lifecycle.dart`: `maxBytes: trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`

Two copies of the MB→bytes shift with the canonical one unused. Either thread `section.requestBlobMaxBytes` through `CliConfig`/`AgentCliConfig` (a `trajectoryRequestBlobMaxBytes` field) so both call sites consume the getter, or drop the getter.

### 5. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:b7059339` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

💡 **SUGGESTION: the config SAVE path (`_trajectoryYaml`) is untested**

The new tests cover parsing (`requestBlobs` defaults, knob validation, strict unknown keys) and `loadProjectTrajectorySection`, but nothing round-trips a save: `_trajectoryYaml()` writes `requestBlobs: false` / non-default knobs only-when-non-default (defaults never written — the file-stays-minimal convention). One assertion like:

```dart
final saved = config.copyWith(trajectoryRequestBlobs: false).toYamlString();
expect(saved, contains('requestBlobs: false'));
```

would pin the save shape (the sibling sections each have one). Low risk — the parse tests would catch a malformed key on the next load — but the asymmetry is free to close.

### 6. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:2b626cf5` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

It widens the diff for anyone bisecting or re-running this file's history. Revert it so the PR stays single-purpose (the local `dart format` version here disagrees with the committed style anyway — the pre-existing lines around it trigger the same delta, so it's a formatter-version artifact, not a real lint fix).

### 7. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:c44f03a2` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (re-raised, still valid on this head): spilled request detail is unreachable from the app UI — only the CLI got a viewer**

This hunk wires spilling into the app host and stubs the buffered detail to role+chars (`preview: ''`, no blocks, `spillFile` pointer), but the app-side readers were not updated:

- `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_details_tabs.dart` `_requestPage` renders `message.preview` (now always `''` for every new session) and `message.blocks` (now always empty) — with no `spillFile` row and no blob resolution. - `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart` (Markdown export, per-message list) has the same dangling-colon shape for spilled sessions.

Net effect: for every new app-hosted session the per-message drill-in data still exists on disk (the blob) but is unreachable from the app — a quiet UX regression the CLI half of this PR solved for itself (`/trajectory inspect` names the blob). Old sessions keep rendering (inline previews intact), so this is degradation, not breakage — hence not blocking.

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key

`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1765
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1765
- **Title**: gh-1745 [PERF] Marathon session files grow to 1GB due to unrotated model_request_summary raw prompt dumps
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1745` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 22
- **Additions**: +1616
- **Deletions**: -62
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T20:38:25Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T00:44:30Z

## PR Description

Refs #1745 (does not close it — see Scope below)
### What changed
- `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`; the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes + rotates the blobs: 50 MB/session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first with the newest always kept; wired into both persist hosts (CLI + app service). `/trajectory inspect` names the blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON; `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (+ `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`, strict section) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path — the capture is never lost, never a crash (same shape as tool-result spilling).
- Replay-safe: the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` basis survives the stubbing; old sessions render as before; `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the blob payload.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

### Scope (gh-1745 closing intent)
- This PR ships the issue's *Proposed Fix* tier: the `model_request_summary` blob offload (658.75 MB of the cited session) with per-session rotation (50 MB / 30-day TTL) plus a boot-time sweep of ended sessions' dirs.
- The **delta-encoding tier** from the issue's own triage comment (99% duplicate payloads, est. 345 MB → ~3.4 MB) is deliberately **not** in this PR — the closing keyword is dropped (`Refs`, not `Closes`) so #1745 stays open for that work.
- The `shell_job_registry` half (215.92 MB) is already bounded for new runs by #1594's persist-window + dedupe — no further work here.

<details><summary>Record flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[".fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json"]
  STORE -->|strip| REC["model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile"]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT["TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept"]
```
</details>

# PR Discussion History

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vfu` — app UI can't reach the spilled request detail

**Fixed** on this head (commit `3f4ef0ad03`).

The app Request tab now surfaces the same pointer the CLI `/trajectory inspect` renders:

- `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_details_tabs.dart` (`_requestPage`) gained a **"Request blob"** row (`strings.requestSpillFile`) rendered whenever `detail.spillFile != null`, grouped with the prompt/manifest hash pointer rows. A new fixture (`spilledAssistant` in `packages/fa_ui/test/trajectory/fixture_details.dart`) pins it: `packages/fa_ui/test/trajectory/trajectory_details_test.dart`, test *"gh-1745: a spilled request names its blob; the stub messages carry no dangling colon"*.
- The tab's inline per-message list skips the empty preview `Text` for stub messages (the text rides the blob) instead of rendering blank lines.
- The dangling-colon renderer is gone from both surfaces the thread named:
  - `_requestSummaryText` (copy-to-clipboard) — new `_requestStubLine` helper emits `role · N chars` with no `: ` tail when `preview.isEmpty`;
  - `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart` Markdown export — same guard; spilled sessions export `- \`user\` 10 chars` (test: `test/trajectory/trajectory_export_test.dart`, *"gh-1745: a spilled request summary exports without dangling colons"*).

Resolution choice: we surface the `spillFile` row rather than resolving the blob content in-tab — the details tabs are pure widgets over the snapshot with no `ExecutionEnv` reach, and the pointer keeps parity with the CLI viewer. Scoping the PR to the CLI host is unnecessary now that the app side has its pointer.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: "Closes #1745" — but `shell_job_registry` (216 MB of the cited ~875 MB) is untouched**

The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. This PR remediates only `model_request_summary`; nothing here touches `shell_job_registry`, so a marathon session still grows unboundedly — just ~4× slower — while the issue auto-closes.

The ticket's Proposed Fix section only describes the `model_request_summary` remediation, so the implementation matches the fix plan — please just confirm the `shell_job_registry` half has a follow-up issue (or extend the blob/TTL policy to it here) so "Closes #1745" doesn't retire the ticket with a quarter of the cited disk growth still open.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `TrajectorySection.requestBlobMaxBytes` is dead code — use it**

The getter (`cli_config.dart:129`) is never referenced: both hosts re-derive the byte budget inline —

- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart`: `maxBytes: config.trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`
- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_lifecycle.dart`: `maxBytes: trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`

Two copies of the MB→bytes shift with the canonical one unused. Either thread `section.requestBlobMaxBytes` through `CliConfig`/`AgentCliConfig` (a `trajectoryRequestBlobMaxBytes` field) so both call sites consume the getter, or drop the getter.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the config SAVE path (`_trajectoryYaml`) is untested**

The new tests cover parsing (`requestBlobs` defaults, knob validation, strict unknown keys) and `loadProjectTrajectorySection`, but nothing round-trips a save: `_trajectoryYaml()` writes `requestBlobs: false` / non-default knobs only-when-non-default (defaults never written — the file-stays-minimal convention). One assertion like:

```dart
final saved = config.copyWith(trajectoryRequestBlobs: false).toYamlString();
expect(saved, contains('requestBlobs: false'));
```

would pin the save shape (the sibling sections each have one). Low risk — the parse tests would catch a malformed key on the next load — but the asymmetry is free to close.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: unrelated reformat of `_CliMessageCapPolicy.learnedCapFor`**

This hunk (`agent_cli.dart`, `_CliMessageCapPolicy`) is pure whitespace/line-wrapping churn — no behavior change, not required by gh-1745. It widens the diff for anyone bisecting or re-running this file's history. Revert it so the PR stays single-purpose (the local `dart format` version here disagrees with the committed style anyway — the pre-existing lines around it trigger the same delta, so it's a formatter-version artifact, not a real lint fix).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (re-raised, still valid on this head): spilled request detail is unreachable from the app UI — only the CLI got a viewer**

This hunk wires spilling into the app host and stubs the buffered detail to role+chars (`preview: ''`, no blocks, `spillFile` pointer), but the app-side readers were not updated:

- `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_details_tabs.dart` `_requestPage` renders `message.preview` (now always `''` for every new session) and `message.blocks` (now always empty) — with no `spillFile` row and no blob resolution. Verified: `grep -rn spillFile packages/fa_ui/lib flutter_app/lib` finds only this writer side.
- `_requestSummaryText` (the Request tab's copy-to-clipboard) renders `'${message.role} · N chars: '` + empty preview → every line ends in a dangling `: `.
- `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart` (Markdown export, per-message list) has the same dangling-colon shape for spilled sessions.

Net effect: for every new app-hosted session the per-message drill-in data still exists on disk (the blob) but is unreachable from the app — a quiet UX regression the CLI half of this PR solved for itself (`/trajectory inspect` names the blob). Old sessions keep rendering (inline previews intact), so this is degradation, not breakage — hence not blocking.

Please add the same pointer to the app Request tab (a `spillFile` row, or resolve the blob via the exported `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore.readDetail`), and fix the two `': '` dangling-colon renderers for the stubbed shape (guard on `preview.isEmpty`).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (re-raised, narrowed after reading the linked issue): "Closes #1745" vs the issue's own triage plan**

The linked issue (github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness#1745, Problem Summary, read this run) cites two unrotated record kinds: `model_request_summary` at **658.75 MB** (1101 records) and `shell_job_registry` at **215.92 MB** (2487 records). The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. This PR remediates only `model_request_summary`; nothing here touches `shell_job_registry`, so a marathon session still grows unboundedly — just ~4× slower — while the issue auto-closes.

The ticket's Proposed Fix section only describes the `model_request_summary` remediation, so the implementation matches the fix plan — please just confirm the `shell_job_registry` half has a follow-up issue (or extend the blob/TTL policy to it here) so "Closes #1745" doesn't retire the ticket with a quarter of the cited disk growth still open.

### 3. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:2a084fc4` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

### 4. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:c9b477ec` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

### 5. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:b7059339` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

💡 **SUGGESTION: the config SAVE path (`_trajectoryYaml`) is untested**

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`

- **PR #**: 1765
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1765
- **Title**: gh-1745 [PERF] Marathon session files grow to 1GB due to unrotated model_request_summary raw prompt dumps
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1745` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 22
- **Additions**: +1616
- **Deletions**: -62
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T20:38:25Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T00:44:30Z

## PR Description

Refs #1745 (does not close it — see Scope below)
### What changed
- `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`; the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes + rotates the blobs: 50 MB/session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first with the newest always kept; wired into both persist hosts (CLI + app service). `/trajectory inspect` names the blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON; `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (+ `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`, strict section) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path — the capture is never lost, never a crash (same shape as tool-result spilling).
- Replay-safe: the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` basis survives the stubbing; old sessions render as before; `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the blob payload.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

### Scope (gh-1745 closing intent)
- This PR ships the issue's *Proposed Fix* tier: the `model_request_summary` blob offload (658.75 MB of the cited session) with per-session rotation (50 MB / 30-day TTL) plus a boot-time sweep of ended sessions' dirs.
- The **delta-encoding tier** from the issue's own triage comment (99% duplicate payloads, est. 345 MB → ~3.4 MB) is deliberately **not** in this PR — the closing keyword is dropped (`Refs`, not `Closes`) so #1745 stays open for that work.
- The `shell_job_registry` half (215.92 MB) is already bounded for new runs by #1594's persist-window + dedupe — no further work here.

<details><summary>Record flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[".fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json"]
  STORE -->|strip| REC["model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile"]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT["TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept"]
```
</details>

# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vfu` — app UI can't reach the spilled request detail

**Fixed** on this head (commit `3f4ef0ad03`).

The app Request tab now surfaces the same pointer the CLI `/trajectory inspect` renders:

- `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_details_tabs.dart` (`_requestPage`) gained a **"Request blob"** row (`strings.requestSpillFile`) rendered whenever `detail.spillFile != null`, grouped with the prompt/manifest hash pointer rows. A new fixture (`spilledAssistant` in `packages/fa_ui/test/trajectory/fixture_details.dart`) pins it: `packages/fa_ui/test/trajectory/trajectory_details_test.dart`, test *"gh-1745: a spilled request names its blob; the stub messages carry no dangling colon"*.
- The tab's inline per-message list skips the empty preview `Text` for stub messages (the text rides the blob) instead of rendering blank lines.
- The dangling-colon renderer is gone from both surfaces the thread named:
  - `_requestSummaryText` (copy-to-clipboard) — new `_requestStubLine` helper emits `role · N chars` with no `: ` tail when `preview.isEmpty`;
  - `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart` Markdown export — same guard; spilled sessions export `- \`user\` 10 chars` (test: `test/trajectory/trajectory_export_test.dart`, *"gh-1745: a spilled request summary exports without dangling colons"*).

Resolution choice: we surface the `spillFile` row rather than resolving the blob content in-tab — the details tabs are pure widgets over the snapshot with no `ExecutionEnv` reach, and the pointer keeps parity with the CLI viewer. Scoping the PR to the CLI host is unnecessary now that the app side has its pointer.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: "Closes #1745" — but `shell_job_registry` (216 MB of the cited ~875 MB) is untouched**

The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. This PR remediates only `model_request_summary`; nothing here touches `shell_job_registry`, so a marathon session still grows unboundedly — just ~4× slower — while the issue auto-closes.

The ticket's Proposed Fix section only describes the `model_request_summary` remediation, so the implementation matches the fix plan — please just confirm the `shell_job_registry` half has a follow-up issue (or extend the blob/TTL policy to it here) so "Closes #1745" doesn't retire the ticket with a quarter of the cited disk growth still open.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `TrajectorySection.requestBlobMaxBytes` is dead code — use it**

The getter (`cli_config.dart:129`) is never referenced: both hosts re-derive the byte budget inline —

- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart`: `maxBytes: config.trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`
- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_lifecycle.dart`: `maxBytes: trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`

Two copies of the MB→bytes shift with the canonical one unused. Either thread `section.requestBlobMaxBytes` through `CliConfig`/`AgentCliConfig` (a `trajectoryRequestBlobMaxBytes` field) so both call sites consume the getter, or drop the getter.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the config SAVE path (`_trajectoryYaml`) is untested**

The new tests cover parsing (`requestBlobs` defaults, knob validation, strict unknown keys) and `loadProjectTrajectorySection`, but nothing round-trips a save: `_trajectoryYaml()` writes `requestBlobs: false` / non-default knobs only-when-non-default (defaults never written — the file-stays-minimal convention). One assertion like:

```dart
final saved = config.copyWith(trajectoryRequestBlobs: false).toYamlString();
expect(saved, contains('requestBlobs: false'));
```

would pin the save shape (the sibling sections each have one). Low risk — the parse tests would catch a malformed key on the next load — but the asymmetry is free to close.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: unrelated reformat of `_CliMessageCapPolicy.learnedCapFor`**

This hunk (`agent_cli.dart`, `_CliMessageCapPolicy`) is pure whitespace/line-wrapping churn — no behavior change, not required by gh-1745. It widens the diff for anyone bisecting or re-running this file's history. Revert it so the PR stays single-purpose (the local `dart format` version here disagrees with the committed style anyway — the pre-existing lines around it trigger the same delta, so it's a formatter-version artifact, not a real lint fix).

### 3. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:2a084fc4` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

Two copies of the MB→bytes shift with the canonical one unused. Either thread `section.requestBlobMaxBytes` through `CliConfig`/`AgentCliConfig` (a `trajectoryRequestBlobMaxBytes` field) so both call sites consume the getter, or drop the getter.

### 5. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-21:b7059339` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-21

The new tests cover parsing (`requestBlobs` defaults, knob validation, strict unknown keys) and `loadProjectTrajectorySection`, but nothing round-trips a save: `_trajectoryYaml()` writes `requestBlobs: false` / non-default knobs only-when-non-default (defaults never written — the file-stays-minimal convention).
